court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
trial_court: Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Court No.4, Lucknow (Matrimonial Case No. 559/2023)
case_name: Arun Pandey vs Smt. Neha Pandey
facts_of_case: Marriage between Arun Pandey and Smt. Neha Pandey was solemnized on 23.01.2011. Out of the said wedlock, one son was born on 05.11.2015. The matrimonial relation became strained and due to indifference, the wife started living separately.

legal_principles.principle: A husband's obligation to maintain his wife arises on marriage, whereas such an obligation towards children arises on their birth.
legal_principles.held: These obligations are imposed on him by operation of law. It is also a moral obligation imposed upon him and it would rather be 'immoral' and 'illegal' to deny them maintenance.

legal_principles.principle: In a matrimonial proceeding, the wife and children are pitted against the husband or father, as the case may be, and in most of the cases they are not on equal footing.
legal_principles.held: Some gets financial support from their parents, brothers and sisters and also some work and earn, in exceptional cases. However, in all cases, the women and children are unable to face the onslaught of matrimonial proceedings because of their financial crisis, which tends to be exploited by the husbands.

legal_principles.principle: The object of Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act in providing maintenance to a party in matrimonial proceedings is obviously to provide financial assistance to the spouse to maintain himself or herself during the pendency of the proceedings and also to have sufficient funds to carry on the litigation so that the spouse does not unduly suffer in the conduct of the case for want of funds.
legal_principles.held: The said provision tends to create a fiction of equality, wherein the wife is tried to brought equally, at least financially along with the husband, so that the matrimonial case initiated is pursued by both the parties suitably & equally.

outcome.final_order: The respondent-wife is directed to pay Rs.50,000/- for legal activities (litigation expenses) and Rs.10,000/- as litigation costs, with a further direction to pay Rs.500/- per hearing within 30 days from the date of order.
